images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of SEE-Forge, the event-driven pipeline for constructing AV-FABLE.Given an event in a pristine video, SEE-Forge plans audio and/or visual manipulations, executes them with editors, and reinserts them into context to create pristine–manipulated twin pairs. The executed interval provides temporal ground truth, while human-reviewed annotations record forensic cues within and around the manipulated event.

Figure 2:Overview of NFSR.(a) Frozen intermediate-layer (“detail”) and interface features pass
through modality-specific gated projection and host-conditioned FiLM.
(b) Independent decoders localize audio and visual manipulations on
separate timelines.
(c) Source-calibrated thresholds give video-level detection and four-way
attribution without changing the intervals.
Audio and video excerpts come from the same clip; intervals are schematic.

Figure 3:Scene diversity in AV-FABLE. Example frames span indoor and
outdoor environments, human activities, objects, food preparation, sports,
and other contexts represented in the twin pairs.

Figure 7:Manipulation examples in AV-FABLE. Each row gives a short
description of the edit, the annotated interval, frames sampled across the
event boundaries, and the local ground-truth (GT) timeline of the
manipulated track; audio rows add the manipulated waveform with the event
shaded. Green and red denote pristine and manipulated content, and frame
borders follow the visual track. Rows (c) and (d) are co-timed events in
one both-track video.

Figure 8:Localization successes and errors. (a) A visual-only object
replacement and (b) an audio-only speech replacement are localized;
(c) a visual object insertion is missed; (d) a pristine video yields a
visual false alarm. Each row shows sampled frames, full-video GT and NFSR
timelines of the displayed track, the annotated and predicted intervals,
and the best tIoU. NFSR intervals are those above the fixed track
threshold; frame borders follow the visual-track GT.

Figure 9:Four asynchronous events in one both-track video. Top: sampled
frames and full-video GT and NFSR timelines for each track, with numbered
GT events. Bottom: each event’s interval and operation/target, pristine
and manipulated frames at the same timestamp (visual) or pristine and
manipulated waveforms over the event window (audio), and the best tIoU.
NFSR matches events 2–4 (tIoU≥0.5\geq 0.5) and misses event 1.

Figure 10:Explanation outputs on fixed NFSR candidates. Each example gives
the annotated track, operation, target, and interval, the tIoU of the
candidate supplied to both modes, and sampled frames. Zero-shot and SFT
panels show the support verdict and the generated inside, context, and
judgment fields; dashes mark empty fields.
